title: Digital Genesis: Computers, Evolution and Artificial Life
text: [1512.02100] Digital Genesis: Computers, Evolution and Artificial Life Skip to main content Search Submit Donate Log in Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Neural and Evolutionary Computing arXiv:1512.02100 (cs) [Submitted on 7 Dec 2015] Title: Digital Genesis: Computers, Evolution and Artificial Life Authors: Tim Taylor , Alan Dorin , Kevin Korb View a PDF of the paper titled Digital Genesis: Computers, Evolution and Artificial Life, by Tim Taylor and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: The application of evolution in the digital realm, with the goal of creating artificial intelligence and artificial life, has a history as long as that of the digital computer itself. We illustrate the intertwined history of these ideas, starting with the early theoretical work of John von Neumann and the pioneering experimental work of Nils Aall Barricelli. We argue that evolutionary thinking and artificial life will continue to play an integral role in the future development of the digital world. Comments: Extended abstract of talk presented at the 7th Munich-Sydney-Tilburg Philosophy of Science Conference: Evolutionary Thinking, University of Sydney, 20-22 March 2014.
